patches.after: "requirement": "SCK is at CPOL level at CSB assertion and before the first edge; edges alternate leading/trailing consistent with CPOL. An SCK change while all CSB are idle and no segment is in progress is an idle-level setup (not a payload edge) only if it moves SCK to the CPOL of an accepted pending segment; otherwise spurious_sck.",

patches.before: **Events.** Starvation/backpressure windows start at segment acceptance so earlier payload faults dirty them. Starvation is triggered when a TX word used by a byte was accepted at or after the boundary edge ending the previous byte; a trace ending at a starved boundary yields a pending event.
patches.after:
**CPOL idle setup.** With all CSB idle and no segment in flight, an SCK change to the pending accepted segment's CPOL level is idle setup: it does not start the segment or count as an edge. Any other unselected SCK change is spurious_sck.

**Events.** Starvation/backpressure windows start at segment acceptance so earlier payload faults dirty them. A starvation episode opens on any row where an in-flight TX segment has sampled all bits of every fetched byte, still needs bytes, and no enabled byte is available non-destructively (exhausted byte-enable cursor counts; pause may precede the trailing edge). It resolves when the next byte is fetched from a refill word (which may be accepted before the postponed edge). Each episode yields an event; unresolved or incomplete episodes are pending.

rationale: Kept LSB-first lanes, pending-CSID handling and all timing/phase checks. CPOL idle setup with all CSB high now only validates against the pending segment's CPOL and no longer pops the segment or shifts edge parity. Starvation now uses a non-destructive enabled-byte peek plus a per-segment sampled-bit count, so a stall after the last sampling edge but before the trailing edge is caught. Episodes open while paused, resolve on the refill fetch and each produce an event; truncated runs are pending and dirty runs fail. New selftests cover these cases.
